chunks: And from him, from Abd al-Rahman, from Hammad ibn Isa, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
He said: My father said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Remember Allah in known days.'
He said: He said: 'The ten [days] of Dhul-Hijjah.'
And he said: 'And numbered days.' He said: 'The days of Tashriq.'

key_terms.أَيَّامٍ مَعْدُودَاتٍ: Numbered days (Quranic phrase referring to specific limited times)
key_terms.أَيَّامٍ مَعْلُومَاتٍ: Known days (Quranic phrase referring to specific sacred times)
key_terms.ذِي الْحِجَّةِ: Dhul-Hijjah (the 12th month of the Islamic calendar)

ai.seo_question: What are the 'known days' and 'numbered days' mentioned in the Quran according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* offers a definitive Shia exegetical link between the Quranic terms 'known days' and 'numbered days' and the sacred period of Dhul-Hijjah, specifically distinguishing the first ten days for general remembrance and the days of Tashriq for specific rituals. It underscores the theological importance of these days in Shia jurisprudence, particularly regarding the expiation (kaffarah) for pilgrims who commit errors or exceed boundaries during Hajj. The chain of narration highlights the continuous transmission of this interpretation from Imam Ali through the Imams, reinforcing its authority in ritual law.
